Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful to see how Acme is planning to use embeddings + reranking for product search and to align on expected traffic levels. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal / scope: real-time product search with embeddings + a lightweight reranker for top-K results; some async batch indexing jobs for nightly re-embeds.
- Integration surface: server-side SDK for query/embeddings, client-side call patterns for search UI, and a backend job for re-embedding.
- Auth: want to confirm Acme prefers API keys (per-service) or a short-lived token flow integrated with your internal auth.
- Routing: recommend routing search queries to the US region (closest), and routing heavy batch jobs to a dedicated pool to avoid impacting real-time SLOs.
- Structured output / tool calling: we'll use Redwood's function-calling for the reranker to return a structured score + provenance metadata.
- Rate limiting & retries: main ask from your infra was how we handle 429s, quotas, and idempotency for non-idempotent operations. See details below and attached quickstart PDF.

1) Can you confirm expected QPS for search queries (avg / peak) and % of traffic that will request embeddings?
2) Procurement: Sam, copying procurement email for timeline on PO/contract items.
3) Marissa will set up a technical deep-dive (SDK walkthrough + sample code) next week — 60min.

Thanks Ben — solid recap. A couple clarifying questions before the deep-dive:

1) Backoff strategy: do you recommend standard exponential backoff with full jitter? Any recommended base/backoff cap and max retries for interactive search requests (we want low latency and graceful degradation).
2) Idempotency: for operations that write to our index (or update user state), what header or request pattern should we use? Do you provide built-in idempotency-key handling?
3) Rate limit headers: what headers does Redwood return on 429s so we can build observability? Also curious whether there's a per-user vs per-account quota and how throttling is prioritized.

Also if you can share a tiny snippet showing retry + idempotency that'd help our infra folks.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Integration & Rate Limit Handling (SDK auth, retries, idempotency)

Alex — great questions. High level answers below; Rishi (SE) and Marissa (proto/demo owner) will cover details in the deep-dive and drop sample code. I've also attached a small idempotency sample (idempotency-sample.js.stub) and linked a Drive doc with more detail.

Backoff / retries:
- Recommendation for interactive search: exponential backoff with full jitter. Typical parameters we recommend: base=100ms, cap=2s, max_retries=5. For latency-sensitive calls prefer fewer retries and surface a degraded response (cached result / fallback) rather than long blocking retries.
- For batch jobs, allow larger caps (up to 10s) and higher retry counts.

Idempotency / request IDs:
- Use a unique Idempotency-Key header for non-idempotent POSTs (e.g., index updates). Redwood will persist the request ID for a short window and ensure the operation is not applied twice. We also accept a client-supplied X-Request-ID for tracing; we echo it in logs and correlate traces.
- Sample header names: Idempotency-Key, X-Request-ID. The SDKs set X-Request-ID automatically; for idempotency you should generate and persist your own Idempotency-Key for retries.

Rate limiting and headers:
- Typical headers returned on throttled responses: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After (seconds). On a 429 we also include a human-readable JSON body with an error.code (e.g., RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) and suggested_retry_after (ms).
- Quotas: we support per-account quotas and optional per-user or per-api-key soft limits. For Dedicated customers we can map quotas to dedicated pools and offer higher limits with SLA.
- Prioritization: requests can be prioritized by token (route) or customer tier; we recommend routing heavier workloads to dedicated pools to avoid impacting realtime SLOs.

SDKs / auth / routing / structured output:
- SDKs: we have server-side clients (Node/Python/Go) that handle automatic retries, request ids, and streaming. They expose hooks to inject Idempotency-Key if you need to control it.
- Auth: API key per service is simplest for server-to-server. For user-scoped flows we recommend short-lived tokens minted by your auth service. We support integration with KMS for key rotation.
- Structured output: use our function/tool-calling feature for reranker responses; you get typed outputs (score, reason, source_id) that make UI integration simpler.
- Embeddings/reranker guidance: batch embedding calls to ~256 items per request for cost/throughput balance; use a separate embeddings pool for bulk indexing. For real-time reranking, call the embedding service for query vectors and the reranker can be a lightweight function call against the top-K.
